edition.locus: Gebhardt VII.XVII (the free supper; Saturus's warning)

source_text: Pridie quoque cum illam caenam ultimam, quam liberam uocant, quantum in ipsis erat non caenam liberam sed agapen caenarent, eadem constantia ad populum uerba iactabant, comminantes iudicium dei, contestantes passionis suae felicitatem, inridentes concurrentium curiositatem, dicente Saturo: Crastinus uobis satis non est, quod libenter uidetis quos odistis? Hodie amici, cras inimici? Notate tamen uobis facies nostras diligenter, ut recognoscatis nos in die illo. Ita omnes inde adtoniti discedebant: ex quibus multi crediderunt.
pass_a_gloss: Also on the day before, when they were eating that last dinner which they call the free one, in so far as it depended on them eating it not as a free dinner but as an agape, with the same firmness they kept throwing words at the crowd, threatening the judgment of God, solemnly affirming the blessedness of their own suffering, jeering at the inquisitiveness of those running together, with Saturus saying: Is the morrow not enough for you, that you gladly look at those whom you hate? Friends today, enemies tomorrow? Nevertheless carefully mark our faces for yourselves, so that you may recognize us in that day. Thus all went away from there stunned, from whom many believed.
pass_b_english: On the day before as well, when they ate that final meal which is called the free one, so far as it lay with them they ate it not as a free feast but as an agape, and with the same steadfastness they hurled words at the people, threatening the judgment of God, bearing witness to the blessedness of their suffering, and laughing to scorn the curiosity of those who flocked together, while Saturus said: Is tomorrow not enough for you, that you willingly gaze upon those whom you hate? Friends today, enemies tomorrow? Yet mark our faces well for yourselves, so that you may know us again on that day.
So they all left that place stunned, and many of them believed.

lemmas.gloss: supper, meal, here the prisoners' last meal
free, in the so-called free dinner

choices.why: liberam agrees with caenam and names the prison custom of a last unrestricted meal; kept as institutional label rather than theological freedom

choices.term: quantum in ipsis erat ... sed agapen
choices.english: so far as it lay with them ... as an agape
choices.why: quantum with erat marks limited agency as prisoners; sed contrasts imposed label with their own act, so agapen kept transliterated as technical Christian term
ablative of time with demonstrative illo points back to iudicium dei without adding a noun not in the Latin; definite but restrained
